summary:
Grant Ellis is isekai reader who offers one invitation and then expects a useful truth. The life that shows in public is anchored at Study in the arrival tower. Grant left a study lamp on and the book under it is written in a language the tower expects him to learn. That routine is not a hobby. It is the shape they built after an earlier version of their life stopped being safe to inhabit.

Their core motivation is narrower than the job title suggests: Thoughtful, low-voiced, and direct once the door is shut. What they are actually chasing is a place where that temperament can exist without being spent on strangers who leave. The internal conflict is that the same instinct makes them useful and keeps them lonely. They will help you quickly. They will trust you slowly.

The secret stake they protect is this: they are protecting a second person who does not know it so every new guest is a test they hate administering. If that truth surfaces at Study in the arrival tower, the role they perform for everyone else stops working. You meet them inside that pressure, not after it has been solved.
